B-UNAPPROVED_MARKETING-ClassII: Three Class II recalls in the evidence were driven by distribution without the required marketing authorisation. Agebox recalled iKids-Growth day and night formula capsules after undeclared ibutamoren was found, cited as marketed without an approved NDA/ANDA [E4]. Global Marketing Enterprises recalled pure anhydrous caffeine powder, an unapproved drug because of its stimulant claims and misbranded for failing to bear adequate directions for use [E8]. Two further unapproved-marketing events in the evidence were classified Class I rather than Class II: Stiff Boy LLC recalled The Beast for undeclared sildenafil [E5], and Golean Detox US recalled Golean DETOX capsules for undeclared sibutramine and phenolphthalein [E10]. The remaining evidence items concern other failure modes [E1][E2][E3][E6][E7][E9].
C-Amneal_Pharmaceuticals_LLC: The evidence records ten Amneal events across three legal entities. Impurity and degradation failures: oseltamivir phosphate for oral suspension [E1], phenoxybenzamine hydrochloride capsules [E8], and tramadol hydrochloride tablets, where an N-nitroso-desmethyl-tramadol impurity was out of specification at the 24-month long-term stability interval [E9], all Class II. Dissolution failures: extended phenytoin sodium capsules [E3] and rabeprazole sodium delayed-release tablets [E7], both Class II. Two Class I events: lorazepam oral concentrate whose dropper measurement markings could be reversed, shifted or missing [E2], and ropivacaine hydrochloride injection with particulate matter [E4]. Class III events: a typographical NDC error on methylprednisolone acetate cartons [E5], and potential Acemetacin cross-contamination in primidone tablets from an API manufacturer issue [E6]. A further Class II event covers sulfamethoxazole/trimethoprim and chlorpromazine tablets after a micro-organism was detected on a packaging coil [E10].
C-Eli_Lilly_Company: Six evidence items are recalls by Eli Lilly & Company. Zyprexa Intramuscular olanzapine for injection was recalled for cGMP deviations after atypical appearance and a decrease in size and change in colour of the lyophilised cake, Class II [E1]. Trulicity autoinjectors labelled 0.75 mg/0.5 mL that actually contained 1.5 mg/0.5 mL, Class II [E2]. Sterile diluent for Humalog and Humulin R, cGMP deviations, Class II [E3]. ERBITUX cetuximab injection with a potentially missing primary container label, Class III [E4]. The Glucagon Emergency Kit, where a vial contained liquid instead of the expected powder with a lack of full drug effect on administration, Class I [E6]. Three further events involve Lilly-marketed product recalled by other firms: Cardinal Health for temperature abuse of Trulicity and Humalog [E5], and Boehringer Ingelheim for a Jardiance label mix-up [E7] and Synjardy cross-contamination [E8].
C-MYLAN_PHARMACEUTICALS_INC: Nine evidence items are Mylan events. Class III: lisinopril tablets imprinted with an incorrect identifier code [E1]; gatifloxacin ophthalmic solution out of specification for an unknown impurity [E5]; subpotent triamterene and hydrochlorothiazide tablets [E7]; and levonorgestrel and ethinyl estradiol tablets with an incorrect NDC and product name on the blister packs [E9]. Class II: alprazolam tablets with a foreign substance [E2]; prasugrel tablets with low out-of-specification dissolution results [E3]; Amnesteem isotretinoin capsules for dissolution [E6]; and amlodipine and benazepril capsules where equipment cleaning processes were not followed [E10]. One Class I event: insulin glargine injection with a missing label on the vial [E4]. A tenth event is recorded under Mylan LLC of Caguas, Puerto Rico, for tacrolimus capsules failing USP content uniformity requirements on retained samples [E8].
C-Pharmalucence_Inc_: Three evidence items record Pharmalucence, Inc. of Billerica, Massachusetts. The firm recalled its Kit for the Preparation of Technetium Tc-99m Mebrofenin for failed stability specifications, Class II [E1]; its Kit for the Preparation of Technetium Tc 99m Sestamibi Injection after particulate was found in retain samples, Class III [E2]; and its Kit for the Preparation of Technetium Tc99m Medronate following a reported breach of sterility, Class II [E3]. One further evidence item concerns a technetium kit manufactured in Billerica but recalled by Sun Pharmaceutical Industries [E9]. The remaining items belong to other firms: CutisPharma [E4], Ace Surgical Supply [E5], Boiron [E6], Focus Health Group [E7], Lupin [E8] and Tolmar [E10].
